items.prompt: An original ecological model for a fictional colony gives the population P(t)=6000/(1+4e^(-0.5t)), where t is measured in years from the start of monitoring. (a) Find P(0). [1] (b) Find the exact time when P(t)=3000, and give your answer to 3 significant figures. [2] (c) Differentiate P(t), and hence calculate the instantaneous population growth rate at t=0. [2] (d) Determine the limiting population as t tends to infinity and explain what this means for the model. [2]
solutionSteps: Taking natural logarithms: -0.5t=ln(1/4)=-ln4; hence t=2ln4=2.772588722... years, or 2.77 years (3 s.f.).
At t=0, P'(0)=12000/25=480 individuals per year.
As t approaches infinity, e^(-0.5t) approaches zero, so P(t) approaches 6000 individuals.
6000 is the model's carrying-capacity limit, not a guarantee about real future populations.

marks.rule: B1 correct initial population 1200
M1 correctly isolate exponential and apply logarithms
A1 exact t=2ln4 and correct 2.77 years
M1 chain/quotient differentiation giving equivalent expression
A1 evaluate 480 individuals/year
B1 limiting value 6000
B1 interpret 6000 as model limit with appropriate caution

items.topic: Complex numbers in polar form and roots
items.calculator: Exact algebra required; verify board calculator policy
items.prompt: Solve z^3=-8i for all complex numbers z. (a) Write -8i in modulus-argument form using a principal argument. [2] (b) Find all three roots, giving answers in exact Cartesian form a+bi. [3] (c) Verify that the sum of your three roots is zero and their product is -8i. [2]
solutionSteps: |-8i|=8 and a principal argument is -π/2, so -8i=8(cos(-π/2)+i sin(-π/2)).
The cube roots have modulus 2 and arguments (-π/2+2πk)/3=-π/6+2πk/3 for k=0,1,2.
For k=1, z=2(cos(π/2)+i sin(π/2))=2i.

marks.rule: B1 modulus 8
B1 principal argument -π/2 and correct polar representation
M1 cube-root modulus 2 and argument formula
A1 two distinct correct exact roots
A1 all three correct exact roots
B1 verify sum zero using stated roots
B1 verify product -8i using stated roots

items.topic: Variable velocity, displacement and total distance
items.calculator: No calculator essential; syllabus mapping and permitted methods require review
items.prompt: A particle moves on a straight line. Its velocity at time t seconds is v(t)=3t^2-12t+9 metres per second for 0≤t≤4. Its initial displacement from a fixed origin is zero. (a) Find the acceleration when t=2. [2] (b) Find the times when the particle is instantaneously at rest. [2] (c) Find the displacement from the origin when t=4. [1] (d) Find the total distance travelled during the first four seconds. [2]
solutionSteps: Acceleration is dv/dt=6t-12 m/s²; at t=2 it is 0 m/s².
At rest, v=0: 3(t²-4t+3)=3(t-1)(t-3)=0, giving t=1 and t=3 seconds.
Displacement from the origin is s(t)=∫v(t)dt=t³-6t²+9t, using s(0)=0.
Because velocity changes sign at t=1 and t=3, total distance must be calculated on each interval.
The displacement is 4 m but the distance is 12 m because the particle reverses direction twice.

marks.rule: M1 differentiate velocity to obtain acceleration
A1 a(2)=0 m/s²
M1 set velocity equal to zero and solve quadratic
A1 t=1,3 seconds
B1 displacement 4 m from correct integral and initial condition
M1 split intervals at both rest times and sum absolute displacement changes
A1 total distance 12 m
